analyzed_videos.description:
*How To Make Force FeedBack Gaming Steering Wheel | Arduino - Build Your Own Racing Experience!*

🏎️ Ready to take your sim racing to the next level? Learn how to create your own DIY force feedback gaming steering wheel with this step-by-step tutorial! 🛠️ 

    In this video, we guide you through the process of creating a custom force feedback steering wheel that will immerse you in the thrilling world of virtual racing. Whether you're a seasoned sim racer or a beginner looking to enhance your setup, this project is perfect for you.👍 

🔧 What You'll Need: 

-Arduino Leonardo Board (This only supports the Leonardo board) 
-BTS7960 Motor Driver 
-775 Motor 
-60T-10mm + 20T-5mm pulley + 200mm close loop belt  
-600ppr Encoder  
-Flexible coupling (10mm to 6mm)  
-10mm Aluminum tube (12Inch)  
-10mm pillow bearing x2  
-L motor bracket  
-L encoder bracket  
-12v fan  
-Power Supply  12v 15A or 20A / 24v 5A
-1k resistor x2 

🎮 *Testing and Gameplay*: You can see how this steering wheel works in some popular games here 

    -Forza Horizon 5 - https://youtu.be/YPjeHWsJ9ZQ?si=Y-NlS9Ifr7cJNLPu 

    -Euro Truck Simulator 2 - https://youtu.be/hmE4mCgDOVo?si=svjCTul2gvQFjJ-X 

🚀 *Why Build Your Own?* 

    -Cost-effective alternative to commercial force feedback wheels. 

    -Customizable to suit your preferences and racing style. 

    -Gain valuable knowledge about force feedback technology and electronics. 

🛠️ *This is how to connect to the PC:*

   Step-by-Step Guide: Connecting a Force Feedback Steering Wheel to Your PC -https://youtu.be/F8xgsbUeE0c?si=CfxVcvSyy_OEpoCn

   Fixed and clarified all issues in RFR wheel configuration (0.21) - https://youtu.be/U0nuY5OHgUA?si=blLdaaSu5cZIpXez

🔗 *Links:*

analyzed_videos.title: DIY Low Budget Gaming Steering Wheel
analyzed_videos.description:
In this video, I'll show you How to make low budget gaming steering wheel.
This is not 100% accurate but you can play with a little disadvantage.

*Some of you have watched my gamepad steering wheel video, which is also a budget steering wheel. However, the steering wheel has a death zone, so this problem has no fix. So I decided to make an Arduino with no death zone and also make it as low-budget as possible. I hope this setup will help someone. Both of the videos I uploaded earlier for pedals are suitable for this, as they both belong to the low-budget category. I'll find out if this can be made even cheaper.*

🔨*Materials Needed*

Arduino leonardo R3 board
KY 040 Encoder
Male-to-female jumper wires
2x 608 2RS Ball Bearing (8x22x7mm)
Nut, Bolt, and washer
8mm thread bar
Rubber flexible tube

*How to Connect to the PC* - ( I'm using EMC Lite software. I previously posted a video on how to connect this software. If you watch the video from 0.53 to 3.44, you can see how to connect this.)
Video Link - https://youtu.be/UUWm1WW1bHI?si=gUQ6_PAl50FalCL5

*DIY Low Budget Gaming Steering Wheel Part 2* (Solution for steering lag) - https://youtu.be/kyhu5ciYFBI?si=__u7jqSxh18t_445
